جَرَّارٌ A man who leads a thousand. (T, end of art. حفز.) ―
-b2- جَيْشٌ جَرَّارٌ, (S, A,) and كَتِيبَةٌ جَرَّارَةٌ, (S, K,) (tropical:) An army, and a troop of horse or the like, that marches heavily, by reason of its numbers: (As, S, K:) or dragging along the apparatus of war: (A:) or numerous. (TA.) ＝
-A2- A potter; a maker of jars, or earthen vessels. (TA. [See جَرَّةٌ.])
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
